items.html: No agent-initiated ask-human / help reply — WAITING for a human reply, the active agent asks (round ≥ 1), same-context resume; a different primitive → L5
No deferred request-rework — a rework intent arriving while parked on a help-ask, stashed as pending_rework_intent and applied by a watchdog → L5 + watchdog (L6/L9)

No resume actions / post-approval mechanics — the resume contract is in (RESUME_WAIT: COMMIT moves commit_pending forward), but the kernel does not run the git commit/merge actions (LC3a), the resource teardown (LC2), or archive (LC4); those + result payloads, retries, and stale-event recovery are later slices. v1 order (reality-checked): APPROVED_FOR_COMMIT → COMMITTED → DONE (commit before DONE), with the merge a separate command after DONE. "Finalization" stays an informal name, not a kernel step type → LC3a · LC2 · LC4

No non-operator resume sources — RESUME_WAIT here is driven by an operator event (COMMIT); internal child-lifecycle resume events arrive at → L4, and timeout / external / fuzzy correlation at → L9, reusing the same contract
No timeout on a human wait — a parked decision waits indefinitely in the MVP; escalation/timeout correlation is later → L9

No multi-channel delivery / rich input forms — the gate already carries a generic decisions map (N keys, per-decision required payload), but the Ask is delivered locally; durable channels and rich forms are later → L8

No dynamic recommendation / decision-condition language — the recommendation is the firing edge's static recommends; a smarter upstream step emitting its own recommendation in its output, and any open predicate language for override/routing beyond the single chosen ≠ recommended rule, are deliberately out → later
No agent-to-agent or external-token ask — only a bound human operator decides here → L7 / L8
